local({
  code <- as.numeric(haven::zap_labels(GUC_Q2))
  other <- lookup_values(GUC_Q2_open1, lookup_respondent_other)
  female <- as.numeric(haven::zap_labels(profile_gender)) == 2
  case_when(
    code %in% c(1, 3) ~ "Mother",
    code %in% c(2, 4) ~ "Father",
    code %in% c(6, 7) ~ "Other carer",
    other %in% "Foster parent" & female ~ "Mother",
    other %in% "Foster parent" ~ "Father",
    !is.na(other) ~ other,
    .default = "Unknown"
  )
})
notes: Respondent's relationship to the child (GUC_Q2, 'Which ONE of the following best describes your relationship with this child?'): mother and step-mother = Mother (1,011), father and step-father = Father (858), grandmother and grandfather = Other carer (32). The 18 'Other' write-ins (GUC_Q2_open1) resolve through the dataset lookup: mother, adoptive mother and foster mother = Mother; dad, father and stepfather = Father; foster carer and foster parent by the panel's recorded sex (2 Mother, 2 Father); grandparent, guardian (4) and uncle = Other carer. Totals 1,018 Mother, 863 Father, 38 Other carer. Six write-ins (three 'Mother', 'Father', 'Dad', 'Stepfather') disagree with the panel's recorded sex (profile_gender) and are taken as written.

local({
  code <- as.numeric(haven::zap_labels(GUC_Q2))
  other <- lookup_values(GUC_Q2_open1, lookup_respondent_other)
  marital <- as.numeric(haven::zap_labels(profile_marital_stat))
  partnered <- marital %in% c(1, 2, 7)
  step <- code %in% c(3, 4) | grepl("step", GUC_Q2_open1, ignore.case = TRUE)
  foster <- grepl("foster", GUC_Q2_open1, ignore.case = TRUE)
  elsewhere <- as.numeric(haven::zap_labels(GUC_Q7b)) %in% 5:8
  case_when(
    elsewhere ~ "Unknown",
    foster ~ "Other",
    code %in% c(6, 7) | other %in% "Other carer" ~ "Unknown",
    step & partnered ~ "Step family",
    step ~ "Unknown",
    partnered ~ "Two biological/adoptive parents",
    marital %in% c(3, 4, 5, 6) ~ "Single parent",
    .default = "Unknown"
  )
})
notes: The respondent's own marital status (profile_marital_stat) read with their relationship to the child (GUC_Q2 and its write-ins GUC_Q2_open1): a step-parent who is married, living as married or in a civil partnership = Step family (58); foster carers = Other (5, no resident biological or adoptive parent); other partnered respondents = Two biological/adoptive parents; separated, divorced, widowed and never married = Single parent; grandparent, guardian and uncle respondents (38), unpartnered step-parents and missing marital status = Unknown, since the data do not record who the child lives with. Respondents who said someone else is the child's primary caregiver (GUC_Q3) and spend 3 days a week or fewer with the child ('Generally, how many days a week do you usually spend with this child?', GUC_Q7b, 70) are also Unknown, as the child's main home is elsewhere. Proximate: marital status forces the category for parents.
